_comment: Sovereign's launch roster (specs/sovereign/leaders-and-art-style.md, Launch roster). Hand-written. Each leader's agenda (what the AI likes and dislikes) is scored in core/src/diplomacy.cpp. Unique units (units, abilities) are rows built on a `base` unit: only what differs is written, the rest comes from the generated Civ data; `uniqueTo` locks them to the civ and they replace their base for it (leaders-and-art-style: Civ abilities, uniques and dynasties). Unique buildings are rows built on a `base` building (whole `yields`, `greatWorkSlots` and `greatPersonPoints` objects are written out since an object replaces the base's); unique improvements are full rows. Unlocks the roster leaves open: Paradise Garden at Early Empire, Beacon Tower at Construction, Nilometer at Irrigation. Leader abilities (`leaderAbility`, Leader details) use the same typed fields as civ abilities. Movement on a kind of ground (the War Chariot on flat land, the Mandinka Lancer in desert, the Chasqui, the Royal Road and Earthshaker on roads) counts where the unit's turn starts, as the Heavy Chariot's does (05); the War Chariot keeps the Heavy Chariot's +1 on open ground. Qin's Builders lay a road on their plot for no charge, which takes their turn (Builders lay no roads in Civ VI, so only his do). Not modelled separately: Augustus's and Cyrus's already-default parts (captured cities keep their buildings). The Legionary's one charge lays a road or builds a Fort (needing no tech of its own, like Civ VI's Roman Fort), and the Legionary stays once it is spent. Approximation: the Repeating Crossbow may also move after attacking.

civilizations.name: England
civilizations.agendaText: Likes civs that keep their fleets away from her coasts; dislikes civs with a navy larger than hers nearby.
civilizations.uniquesText: Longbowman (replaces Crossbowman): +5 Ranged Strength attacking from hills or woods, 10% cheaper. Mill Town (replaces Factory): +1 Housing, +1 Production to adjacent mines.
civilizations.voice: Shrewd, witty and guarded; proud of her navy and her independence; speaks with regal poise and dry humour.

ability.name: Mills and Mines
ability.text: Iron and Coal mines +1 Production; Industrial Zones +1 Production adjacency from a Harbor.

leaderAbility.name: Sea Dogs
leaderAbility.text: +25% Production toward naval units; +50% Great Admiral points; trade routes to another continent +2 Gold.

civilizations.name: France
civilizations.agendaText: Likes civs following his religion; dislikes civs converting his cities.
civilizations.uniquesText: Scara (replaces Knight): +1 Movement, heals 10 HP when it kills a unit. Royal Abbey (replaces Temple): +1 Science and +1 Culture.
civilizations.voice: Pious, ambitious and commanding; sees himself as protector of the faith and of learning; speaks plainly, like a soldier-king.

ability.name: Cathedral Builders
ability.text: +15% Production toward Medieval and Renaissance wonders; each wonder +1 Amenity in its city.

leaderAbility.name: Carolingian Renaissance
leaderAbility.text: Holy Site buildings also give +1 Science and +1 Culture; heavy cavalry +3 Combat Strength within 2 tiles of the leader.

civilizations.name: Rome
civilizations.agendaText: Likes civs at peace; dislikes warmongers.
civilizations.uniquesText: Legionary (replaces Swordsman): +4 Combat Strength, one Builder charge for roads and forts. Forum (replaces Market): +1 Amenity and +1 Gold per trade route from the city.
civilizations.voice: Calm, calculating and statesmanlike; prizes order, peace on his terms and grand works; speaks with measured authority.

ability.name: Colonia
ability.text: New cities start with +1 Population and a free Monument.

leaderAbility.name: City of Marble
leaderAbility.text: +20% Production toward City Center buildings and wonders; +1 Amenity in every city with an established governor.

civilizations.name: Greece
civilizations.agendaText: Respects civs with strong armies; scorns civs with weak ones.
civilizations.uniquesText: Hoplite (replaces Spearman): +10 Combat Strength next to another Hoplite. Odeon (replaces Amphitheater): +1 Great Work of Writing slot, +1 Envoy when built.
civilizations.voice: Blunt, laconic and fearless; respects strength and courage, scorns softness; uses few words.

ability.name: Polis
ability.text: +2 Culture per city-state you are suzerain of; Theater Squares +1 adjacency from an Encampment.

leaderAbility.name: Hold the Pass
leaderAbility.text: Melee and anti-cavalry units +5 Combat Strength defending on hills or in a district; +1 Culture per Encampment building.

civilizations.name: Persia
civilizations.agendaText: Likes civs that spare the cities they take; hates civs that raze them.
civilizations.uniquesText: Immortal (replaces Swordsman): can also make a ranged attack (strength 25). Paradise Garden (improvement): +2 Culture, +1 Amenity, raises nearby Appeal.
civilizations.voice: Magnanimous, worldly and persuasive; respects other peoples and their customs; speaks generously but never forgets a slight.

ability.name: Satrapies
ability.text: Cities with an established governor +2 Loyalty and +2 Gold; +1 Governor title at Political Philosophy.

leaderAbility.name: King of Kings
leaderAbility.text: Captured cities keep their buildings and get +5 Loyalty a turn; +1 Amenity in your cities of another religion; roads +1 Movement in your territory.

civilizations.name: Arabia
civilizations.agendaText: Likes civs that wage war honourably and keep the peace; hates civs that send assassins.
civilizations.uniquesText: Mamluk (replaces Knight): heals every turn, even after moving or attacking. Madrasa (replaces University): +2 Faith, +1 Great Scientist point.
civilizations.voice: Chivalrous, devout and honourable; keeps his word and expects others to keep theirs; speaks with courtesy and gravity.

ability.name: Caravan Cities
ability.text: Trade routes through desert +2 Gold; Campuses +1 adjacency from a Commercial Hub.

leaderAbility.name: Chivalry of the Sultan
leaderAbility.text: Units +4 Combat Strength within 2 tiles of a city following your religion; Holy Site buildings +1 Science.

civilizations.name: China
civilizations.agendaText: Dislikes civs that build wonders before him.
civilizations.uniquesText: Repeating Crossbow (replaces Crossbowman): can attack after moving. Beacon Tower (improvement, own borders): +1 Culture, +2 vision, +4 Combat Strength to units defending on it.
civilizations.voice: Imperious, impatient and visionary; demands order and obedience; speaks as the first and only emperor.

ability.name: Imperial Examinations
ability.text: Each Governor title gives +1 Science and +1 Culture in the capital.

leaderAbility.name: Standardization
leaderAbility.text: Builders +1 charge; +50% Production toward walls; Builders lay a road on their tile without using a charge.

civilizations.name: Japan
civilizations.agendaText: Dislikes civs that send missionaries or traders into his territory.
civilizations.uniquesText: Samurai (replaces Man-At-Arms): no Combat Strength loss when damaged. Castle Town (replaces Medieval Walls): +2 Housing, +1 Culture.
civilizations.voice: Patient, cautious and reserved; values peace, stability and keeping foreigners at a distance; speaks politely and sparingly.

ability.name: Craft Guilds
ability.text: Industrial Zones and Theater Squares +1 adjacency from each other.

leaderAbility.name: Edo Peace
leaderAbility.text: At peace with every major civ: +10% Science and Culture in all cities; Encampment buildings +1 Amenity in their city.

civilizations.name: Egypt
civilizations.agendaText: Dislikes civs with more wonders than he has.
civilizations.uniquesText: War Chariot (replaces Heavy Chariot): +1 Movement on flat land, no movement cost to attack. Nilometer (improvement, river tiles): +1 Food to adjacent Farms, halves flood damage nearby.
civilizations.voice: Grandiose and proud; obsessed with monuments and a name that will last forever; speaks in lofty, boastful terms.

ability.name: Gift of the Nile
ability.text: Districts and wonders can be built on floodplains with no penalty; river tiles +1 Food.

leaderAbility.name: Builder of Monuments
leaderAbility.text: Wonders +2 Culture; +15% Production toward wonders; light cavalry and chariots +5 Combat Strength on flat desert and floodplains.

civilizations.name: Mali
civilizations.agendaText: Likes civs that send trade routes to him; dislikes civs that plunder traders.
civilizations.uniquesText: Mandinka Lancer (replaces Knight): +1 Movement in desert, +5 Combat Strength against units in desert. Sahel Mosque (replaces Temple): +2 Gold, +1 Housing.
civilizations.voice: Generous, wealthy and devout; loves trade and fair dealing; speaks warmly, often of gold and pilgrimage.

ability.name: Saharan Riches
ability.text: Mines on desert and desert hills +2 Gold; Commercial Hubs +1 adjacency per 2 adjacent desert tiles.

leaderAbility.name: Golden Pilgrimage
leaderAbility.text: International trade routes +2 Gold and +1 Faith; Commercial Hub buildings can be bought with Faith.

civilizations.name: Aztec
civilizations.agendaText: Respects civs that declare war formally; hates surprise wars.
civilizations.uniquesText: Jaguar Warrior (replaces Warrior): +4 Combat Strength in woods and rainforest, captures defeated units as Builders. Calmecac (replaces Library): +1 Faith, +25% XP for units trained in the city.
civilizations.voice: Fierce, devout and proud; honours open challenges and despises treachery; speaks with intensity.

ability.name: Chinampas
ability.text: Farms next to a lake or river +1 Food and +0.5 Housing.

leaderAbility.name: Flower Wars
leaderAbility.text: Killing an enemy unit grants Faith equal to half its Combat Strength; +1 Amenity in the capital per 3 enemy units killed this era (up to +3).

civilizations.name: Inca
civilizations.agendaText: Dislikes civs that settle in the mountains near him.
civilizations.uniquesText: Chasqui (replaces Scout): +1 Movement, +1 more on roads. Qullqa (replaces Granary): +2 Housing, +1 Food per adjacent mountain (up to +2).
civilizations.voice: Ambitious, practical and territorial about his mountains; values roads, terraces and order; speaks firmly.

ability.name: Mit'a Labor
ability.text: +20% Production toward districts in cities next to a mountain; mountain tiles can be worked for +2 Production.

leaderAbility.name: Earthshaker
leaderAbility.text: Roads on hills and next to mountains +1 Movement; +1 Housing in cities next to a mountain; Farms on hills +1 Food.
